lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Clarify the résumé’s target and move relevant research, technical skills, and publications higher for quant roles.
items.because: The Ph.D. and research work are the strongest qualifications for quantitative research roles.

items.says: Shorten or reduce the visual prominence of the bakery role unless it serves a leadership, operations, or employment-continuity purpose.
items.because: It is not directly relevant to quant research.

items.says: Order the Northpeak bullets by credibility and relevance rather than chronology or dramatic impact.
items.because: Northpeak is the most important section for quant applications.

items.says: Clarify whether the Ph.D. is full-time given the overlapping employment dates.
items.because: The overlap could raise questions.

items.says: Give the working papers, under-review manuscript, seminar presentation, and open-source package a separate research-output section.
items.because: These outputs deserve more visibility.

items.says: Use consistent date ranges, separators, capitalization, and bullet punctuation throughout.
Fix awkward bullet wrapping and alignment in the final PDF.
items.because: Several bullets break awkwardly and may create excessive white space.

items.says: Confirm that the Northpeak details comply with confidentiality policies.
items.because: The résumé discloses desk results, portfolio-manager approval, live allocation, and internal project reuse.

items.says: Replace the placeholder website and link directly to a relevant code, research, or professional profile.
items.because: A nonfunctional or generic URL undermines the application.

items.says: Consider adding one useful LinkedIn, Google Scholar, research-page, or GitHub link.
items.because: Profiles with little useful content should not all be added.

items.says: Add a research focus, advisor, dissertation topic, specialization, or relevant coursework if it strengthens the candidacy.
items.because: The entry currently gives no specialization for the strongest quant qualification.

items.says: Verify that the candidacy status and Expected May 2026 date are still accurate.
items.because: The entry should be updated if the candidate has defended, advanced, or changed the expected date.

items.says: Consider removing the B.S. if space is tight and it adds nothing beyond the Ph.D.
items.because: The undergraduate degree is less important than publications, methods, and technical work.

items.says: Specify scheduling authority, budget size, staffing complexity, or another measurable operational result.
items.because: Managed and keeping within budget are credible but generic, and the direct responsibility is unclear.

items.says: Use a spelling convention for labour that is consistent with the country and employer.
Add the period over which unsold bread fell from 12% to 7%.
items.because: Without a timeframe, the result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction came solely from this process or from a broader store initiative.
items.because: Cutting may overstate causality if other changes contributed.

items.says: Define risk-adjusted returns and give the baseline, evaluation period, evaluation setting, costs, and relevant capacity assumptions.
items.because: Without those details, the 35% improvement may look loosely defined or overfit.

items.says: Clarify whether the 35% claim is another presentation of the later Sharpe improvement.
items.because: Multiple versions of the same result should not be reported unless they measure distinct outcomes.

items.says: Specify what was purged, why the embargo length was appropriate, and whether tuning and evaluation were fully separated.
items.because: Those details are needed to establish the rigor of the validation design.

items.says: Revise the absolute claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: Purging and embargoing reduce leakage risks but do not automatically prove the absence of look-ahead bias.

items.says: Consider stating the number of folds or train/test structure.
items.because: That information may further demonstrate methodological rigor.

items.says: Clarify the candidate’s role in designing the point-in-time safeguards and name the technical environment if relevant.
Verify that feature store accurately describes the implementation.
items.because: It may instead have been a library, pipeline, database, or research framework.

items.says: Clarify whether the live allocation actually occurred, the candidate’s monitoring role, and what small means if disclosure rules permit.
items.because: Approved and live allocation can attract scrutiny and should be precise and compliant.

items.says: Align the tense and timing of the allocation with the internship dates.
items.because: If it happened after the internship, the candidate’s involvement must be stated accurately.

items.says: The best Sharpe among 400 searched configurations is presented as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: This creates selection and multiple-testing bias and is not an unbiased estimate of future performance.

items.says: The order-book signal result appears duplicated in the Kaggle project.
items.because: It may claim the same accomplishment twice or imply inconsistent ownership.

items.says: Clarify ownership, chronology, individual contribution, and the relationship between the signal and the desk book.
items.because: Desk book impact is portfolio-level, while built a signal implies an individual research contribution.

items.says: Add the benchmark, observations or trades, and whether the 18-month period was genuinely untouched during development.
Using the same random seed on every worker can create duplicated or correlated random streams.
items.because: That can invalidate the Monte Carlo simulation.

items.says: Verify that the speed comparison held simulation quality and hardware constant.
Clarify authorship, contribution, and manuscript status without implying acceptance.
items.because: Under review is not the same as publication.

items.says: Emphasize the significance and scope of the contribution rather than its location in Section 3.
items.because: The current wording emphasizes the paper’s location instead of the contribution.

items.says: Confirm that by a log factor is mathematically accurate and supported by the paper and advisor.
items.because: The phrase can be interpreted differently depending on the exact bound.

items.says: Add a public manuscript link if available.
items.because: Links make technical claims more credible.

items.says: Shorten or deprioritize the teaching bullet for industry quant applications.
items.because: It is less relevant than modeling, research, and production-oriented work.

items.says: State who provided the 4.8/5 rating and give the response rate.
items.because: Otherwise the rating may appear selectively reported.

items.says: Add the package name and a link if it is public.
items.because: The accomplishment is currently difficult to validate.

items.says: Clarify the download source and whether 3,000 means users, downloads, or repository events.
items.because: The current wording does not define the metric.

items.says: Consider emphasizing testing, documentation, maintenance, or external adoption instead of raw downloads.
items.because: Those may be more meaningful measures of the package’s impact.

items.says: Specify the forecast horizon, evaluation period, data frequency, information sets, and tuning procedures.
items.because: The context is needed to distinguish a robust result from a favorable setup or arbitrary split.

items.says: Clarify that the test data were not used for architecture, feature, or hyperparameter decisions.
items.because: That is required for the out-of-sample description to be credible.

items.says: Clarify whether the crisis-period tests were included in the Holm correction and whether forecast-error dependence was handled appropriately.
Clarify whether both crisis periods were specified in advance.
items.because: Otherwise the result may appear selectively emphasized.

items.says: Distinguish statistical significance from economic significance.
items.because: A significant QLIKE improvement does not necessarily imply trading value.

items.says: Add a paper link and specify the candidate’s presentation role if there were coauthors.
items.because: This would better establish availability and individual contribution.

items.says: Replace the 12-page detail with the paper’s title, status, or availability.
items.because: The page count adds little value.

items.says: Add a notable outcome such as rank, score, team result, dataset scale, or technical constraint.
items.because: The current description is generic and does not distinguish the work from routine modeling.

items.says: Explain which direction the validation gap moved and why time-grouped folds were appropriate.
items.because: The revised methodology and its justification matter more than the numerical gap.

items.says: Avoid implying that closing the leaderboard gap proves the validation scheme was correct.
items.because: Leaderboard alignment is not itself proof of valid evaluation.

items.says: The order-book imbalance result appears duplicated from the Northpeak internship.
items.because: The same 18-month Sharpe improvement seems to be claimed in two places.

items.says: Confirm that the futures-book result was actually part of the Kaggle project and that the candidate may describe it.
items.because: It appears to claim professional portfolio impact inside a competition project.

items.says: Clarify that the data and signal were not reused from the internship.
items.because: The overlap creates a serious ownership and credibility problem.

items.says: Organize the skills by proficiency or relevance.
Include important quant tools or libraries demonstrated elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Relevant tools may be missing from the current list.

items.says: Kafka is not supported elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Unsupported skills can look like keyword padding.

items.says: Make the depth of the listed PyTorch experience clear in the project section.
items.because: A listed technology should be supportable in a technical interview.

items.says: Econometircs is misspelled and should be econometrics.
items.because: The typo is particularly damaging in a stated area of expertise.

items.says: Use consistent capitalization and formatting in the methods category.
Consider adding demonstrated methods such as volatility forecasting, time-series validation, point-in-time handling, multiple-testing correction, and statistical learning.
items.because: The current list omits methods clearly shown elsewhere in the résumé.
